annotations.description: Marks this Ingress as the canary (alternative backend) of the main Ingress with the same host and path.
Request header that sends traffic to the canary when its value is 'always' and never when 'never'; other values fall through to the next rule.
Exact value of the canary-by-header header that routes to the canary; requires canary-by-header.
PCRE regex matched against the canary-by-header value; ignored when canary-by-header-value is set.
Cookie that sends traffic to the canary when its value is 'always' and never when 'never'.
Share of random requests (0 to canary-weight-total) sent to the canary; precedence is header, then cookie, then weight.
Total weight against which canary-weight is computed.
URI the matched path is rewritten to before proxying (regex capture groups such as $2 allowed); forces regex location matching for all paths of the host.
Treats the Ingress paths as case-insensitive regular expressions; the regex modifier then applies to every path of the host.
Redirects requests for '/' to this application root path (HTTP 302).
Returns a permanent redirect to this URL instead of proxying (301 unless permanent-redirect-code is set).
Status code used by permanent-redirect.
Returns a temporary redirect to this URL instead of proxying (302 unless temporal-redirect-code is set).
Status code used by temporal-redirect (custom code support added in v1.12.0, PR #10651).
Redirects between www.<host> and <host>; the direction depends on the host declared in the Ingress.
Redirects HTTP to HTTPS (http-redirect-code, default 308) when the Ingress has TLS; 'false' disables it for this Ingress (global default: ConfigMap ssl-redirect).
Redirects HTTP to HTTPS even when the Ingress has no TLS section (TLS terminated in front of NGINX).
Keeps the trailing slash of the URI when redirecting to HTTPS.
Comma-separated extra server_name values for the host; ignored when an alias collides with an existing host.
Overrides the Host header sent to the backend (default $host).
Adds the non-standard X-Forwarded-Prefix header with this value to the backend request.
Makes redirects issued by NGINX relative (absolute_redirect off); global default from ConfigMap relative-redirects; not described in annotations.md.
Includes the port in absolute redirects issued by NGINX (port_in_redirect); global default from the ConfigMap key of the same name; not described in annotations.md.
Enables HTTP authentication of type 'basic' or 'digest'.
Secret (name or namespace/name) holding the basic/digest credentials.
Format of auth-secret: 'auth-file' (htpasswd in key 'auth') or 'auth-map' (one key per user).
Realm text shown in the basic/digest authentication challenge.
URL of an external authentication service called through an auth subrequest for each request (2xx allows, 401/403 deny).
HTTP method used for the auth-url subrequest.
URL the client is redirected to when external authentication returns 401.
Query parameter of the auth-signin URL that carries the original URL (the template falls back to 'rd').
Comma-separated headers copied from the auth response to the backend request.
Value of the X-Auth-Request-Redirect header sent to the auth service.
ConfigMap (namespace/name) of headers sent to the auth service.
Enables caching of auth responses with this key (for example $remote_user$http_authorization).
Cache validity per auth response code (proxy_cache_valid syntax, comma-separated list).
Max idle keepalive connections to the auth-url upstream (0 disables; no variables allowed in the URL host; docs say it does not work with the HTTP/2 listener).
Shares NGINX variables between the request and the auth subrequest (for example the same X-Request-ID).
Max requests served through one keepalive connection to the auth service (when auth-keepalive > 0).
Idle timeout in seconds of keepalive connections to the auth service (when auth-keepalive > 0).
Sets cookies returned by the auth request even when the upstream status is not 200, 201, 204, 206, 301, 302, 303, 304, 307 or 308.
Custom NGINX directives for the external auth location (used only with auth-url); snippet.
'false' exempts this Ingress from the ConfigMap global-auth-url external authentication.
'any' lets a request pass when any one access check succeeds (for example IP allow-list or auth) instead of all of them.
Secret (namespace/name) whose ca.crt verifies client certificates (mTLS); applies per host, not per path.
Client certificate verification mode: on, off, optional or optional_no_ca.
Maximum verification depth of the client certificate chain.
URL or named location the user is redirected to when client certificate authentication fails.
Passes the client certificate (PEM, URL-encoded) to the backend in the ssl-client-cert header.
Regex the client certificate subject must match (value starts with 'CN='); 403 otherwise.
Sends the TLS connection unterminated to the backend (L4); requires --enable-ssl-passthrough and makes all other annotations of the Ingress ineffective.
ssl_ciphers for the host server block (default: ConfigMap ssl-ciphers).
Sets ssl_prefer_server_ciphers on or off for the host server block (default: inherited from the http context).
Protocol used to reach the backend: HTTP, HTTPS, AUTO_HTTP, GRPC, GRPCS or FCGI (case-insensitive).
Secret (namespace/name) with tls.crt/tls.key (client certificate) and ca.crt used for TLS to the backend.
Verifies the backend server certificate ('on' or 'off').
Verification depth of the backend certificate chain.
OpenSSL cipher list for TLS connections to the backend.
TLS protocol versions enabled for connections to the backend.
Server name used to verify the backend certificate and sent as SNI (proxy_ssl_name).
Sends SNI to the backend ('on' or 'off').
Max concurrent connections from one client IP, per controller replica (limit-conn-status-code, default 503, when exceeded).
Max requests per second from one client IP, per controller replica; burst = limit x limit-burst-multiplier (limit-req-status-code, default 503).
Max requests per minute from one client IP, per controller replica; burst = limit x limit-burst-multiplier.
Burst multiplier applied to limit-rps, limit-rpm and limit-connections.
Response bandwidth per connection, rendered as limit_rate <n>k (kilobytes per second); 0 disables; needs proxy-buffering on; default from ConfigMap limit-rate.
Kilobytes sent at full speed before limit-rate applies (limit_rate_after <n>k); needs proxy-buffering on; default from ConfigMap limit-rate-after.
Comma-separated client CIDRs exempt from limit-rps, limit-rpm and limit-connections; not described in annotations.md (which documents limit-whitelist).
Legacy alias of limit-allowlist, read only when limit-allowlist is empty; the name documented in annotations.md.

Legacy alias of allowlist-source-range, read only when allowlist-source-range is empty; the name documented in annotations.md.
Comma-separated client CIDRs denied (403); overrides the ConfigMap denylist-source-range.

Number of endpoints in each hash subset.

HTTP version used towards the backend ('1.0' or '1.1').
Overrides the Connection header sent to the backend (validated to 'close' or 'keep-alive').

Enables session affinity; the only supported type is 'cookie'.
'balanced' redistributes some sessions when the deployment scales up; 'persistent' never rebalances.

'true' re-pins the cookie to another endpoint after a failed attempt; 'false' keeps the sticky endpoint.
Rewrites the Domain attribute of Set-Cookie headers from the backend ('off' or 'source replacement').
Rewrites the Path attribute of Set-Cookie headers from the backend.
Enables CORS handling (preflight responses and CORS response headers).

keyFacts: kubernetes/ingress-nginx is archived (GitHub API archived=true, last push 2026-03-23) and its last release is controller-v1.15.1, published 2026-03-19 together with v1.14.5 and v1.13.9, so v1.15.1 is the final baseline for the key catalog. https://github.com/kubernetes/ingress-nginx/releases/tag/controller-v1.15.1

The README at controller-v1.15.1 says best-effort maintenance ran until March 2026 and that there will be no further releases, bugfixes or security fixes, while existing images and Helm charts remain available. https://github.com/kubernetes/ingress-nginx/blob/controller-v1.15.1/README.md

v1.15.1 parses 136 annotation keys (risk: 5 Critical, 10 High, 45 Medium, 76 Low; scope: 48 ingress, 88 location) plus 2 legacy aliases, whitelist-source-range (of allowlist-source-range) and limit-whitelist (of limit-allowlist), read only when the primary key is empty: 138 keys to recognise. https://github.com/kubernetes/ingress-nginx/blob/controller-v1.15.1/docs/user-guide/nginx-configuration/annotations-risk.md

annotations.md is incomplete: its summary table lists 117 keys, 21 parsed keys are missing from it and 8 are not mentioned anywhere in it (allowlist-source-range, limit-allowlist, relative-redirects, use-port-in-redirects, disable-proxy-intercept-errors, opentelemetry-operation-name, fastcgi-index, fastcgi-params-configmap); the generated annotations-risk.md is the complete list. https://github.com/kubernetes/ingress-nginx/blob/controller-v1.15.1/docs/user-guide/nginx-configuration/annotations.md

The annotation prefix is set by --annotations-prefix (default nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io); with a custom prefix the admission check rejects Ingresses that still use nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/* keys, so the inventory must read the controller args before matching keys. https://github.com/kubernetes/ingress-nginx/blob/controller-v1.15.1/internal/ingress/controller/controller.go

Since v1.12.0 the defaults are hardened: annotations-risk-level High (Critical annotations rejected), allow-cross-namespace-resources false, strict-validate-path-type true, --enable-annotation-validation true, --enable-metrics false; global rate limiting and third-party Lua plugins were removed in the same release. https://github.com/kubernetes/ingress-nginx/blob/controller-v1.15.1/changelog/controller-1.12.0.md

allow-snippet-annotations defaults to false and the admission check then rejects every annotation whose key ends in -snippet; the 5 Critical annotations are configuration-snippet, server-snippet, stream-snippet, auth-snippet and modsecurity-snippet, so working snippets mean both guard rails were deliberately relaxed. https://github.com/kubernetes/ingress-nginx/blob/controller-v1.15.1/internal/ingress/controller/controller.go

12 annotation keys were removed since v1.0: enable-influxdb, influxdb-measurement, influxdb-port, influxdb-host, influxdb-server-name and secure-verify-ca-secret (v1.7.1), enable-opentracing and opentracing-trust-incoming-span (OpenTracing dropped, v1.10.0), global-rate-limit, global-rate-limit-window, global-rate-limit-key and global-rate-limit-ignored-cidrs (v1.12.0). https://github.com/kubernetes/ingress-nginx/tree/controller-v1.15.1/changelog

The v1.15.1 admission webhook still returns 'annotation ... is deprecated' warnings for the five influxdb keys and secure-verify-ca-secret, none of which has any effect any more. https://github.com/kubernetes/ingress-nginx/blob/controller-v1.15.1/internal/ingress/controller/controller.go

http2-push-preload is still parsed and rendered as http2_push_preload, but NGINX removed HTTP/2 server push in 1.25.1 (the directive is ignored with a warning) and the v1.15.1 image builds NGINX 1.27.1, so the annotation is a no-op. https://nginx.org/en/docs/http/ngx_http_v2_module.html

The v1.15.1 ConfigMap decoder accepts 196 keys while configmap.md's table has 192 rows: 14 accepted keys are undocumented (e.g. disable-http-access-log, enable-auth-access-log, forwarded-host-header, proxy-http-version, use-port-in-redirects, disable-proxy-intercept-errors), 2 are internal (bind-address-ipv4/ipv6), and 14 documented keys no longer exist (use-geoip and 13 jaeger-* keys). https://github.com/kubernetes/ingress-nginx/blob/controller-v1.15.1/internal/ingress/controller/config/config.go

36 ConfigMap keys were removed since v1.0: all OpenTracing, Zipkin, Jaeger and Datadog keys (gone by v1.10.0), use-geoip (legacy GeoIP, v1.9.3), the six global-rate-limit-* keys and plugins (v1.12.0). https://github.com/kubernetes/ingress-nginx/tree/controller-v1.15.1/changelog

ConfigMap http2-max-field-size, http2-max-header-size and http2-max-requests are documented as deprecated and map to NGINX directives obsolete since 1.19.7 (large_client_header_buffers and keepalive_requests replace them). https://nginx.org/en/docs/http/ngx_http_v2_module.html

limit-rate and limit-rate-after (annotation and ConfigMap) are rendered as 'limit_rate <n>k' and 'limit_rate_after <n>k', i.e. kilobytes, although configmap.md and the code comments say bytes per second. https://github.com/kubernetes/ingress-nginx/blob/controller-v1.15.1/internal/ingress/controller/template/template.go

limit-rps, limit-rpm and limit-connections apply per controller replica, so the effective limit is multiplied by the replica count (and moves with HPA); burst = limit x limit-burst-multiplier (default 5). https://github.com/kubernetes/ingress-nginx/blob/controller-v1.15.1/docs/user-guide/nginx-configuration/annotations.md

Global defaults every Ingress inherits and that change silently on migration: ssl-redirect true with http-redirect-code 308, proxy-body-size 1m, proxy-connect-timeout 5 s, proxy-read/send-timeout 60 s, proxy-buffering off, proxy-request-buffering on, HSTS on (max-age 31536000, includeSubDomains), ssl-protocols TLSv1.2 TLSv1.3, use-forwarded-headers false, keep-alive 75 s. https://github.com/kubernetes/ingress-nginx/blob/controller-v1.15.1/internal/ingress/controller/config/config.go

ConfigMap app-root and upstream-hash-by* are accepted by the decoder but have no global consumer in the v1.15.1 code, while the undocumented keys use-port-in-redirects, preserve-trailing-slash, proxy-http-version, proxy-max-temp-file-size and proxy-redirect-to do act as global defaults for their annotations. https://github.com/kubernetes/ingress-nginx/blob/controller-v1.15.1/internal/ingress/defaults/main.go

The controller defines 72 flags in pkg/flags/flags.go plus 15 klog flags; none was removed between v1.0.0 and v1.15.1 (22 were added); cli-arguments.md omits --profiler-address, and --ingress-class (default nginx) is marked '[IN DEPRECATION]'. https://github.com/kubernetes/ingress-nginx/blob/controller-v1.15.1/pkg/flags/flags.go

Microsoft Learn: managed NGINX of the AKS application routing add-on stops receiving Azure support after November 2026, and the appRoutingGateway implementation (GatewayClass approuting-istio) cannot configure request header/body size limits, Lua or local/global rate limiting and does not support EnvoyFilter, so limit-* annotations, proxy-body-size and header-buffer keys have no appRoutingGateway equivalent. https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/aks/app-routing-gateway-api

The docs site kubernetes.github.io/ingress-nginx still answered HTTP 200 on 2026-11-04, and annotations.md, annotations-risk.md, configmap.md and cli-arguments.md are byte-identical on main and at controller-v1.15.1. https://kubernetes.github.io/ingress-nginx/user-guide/nginx-configuration/annotations/
uncertainties: OpenTracing annotation removal: the changelog flags it as a v1.10.0 breaking change, but the parser is already absent from the controller-v1.9.5 tag (present at v1.9.4) and the 1.9.5 changelog is silent. The catalog marks the keys as removed either way.

Removed-since-v1.0 lists come from the changelogs plus source snapshots at v1.0.0, v1.9.4, v1.11.8 and v1.15.1; a key added and removed between two snapshots without a changelog note would be missed (none is known).

http2-push-preload being a no-op is inferred from NGINX source/docs and NGINX_VERSION=1.27.1 in build.sh; it was not tested at runtime, the ingress-nginx docs do not flag it, and the first ingress-nginx release shipping NGINX >= 1.25.1 was not identified (v1.10.0 shipped NGINX 1.25.0).
limit-rate units conflict: annotations.md says kilobytes, configmap.md and code comments say bytes per second; resolved from template.go (renders a 'k' suffix), not tested at runtime.
ConfigMap app-root and upstream-hash-by* having no global effect is based on code reading of v1.15.1 only (UNVERIFIED at runtime).

Some defaults are effective rather than literal struct defaults: load-balance round_robin (Lua DEFAULT_LB_ALG), affinity-mode balanced and affinity-canary-behavior sticky (documented; the parser stores an empty string), ssl-prefer-server-ciphers (inherited from the http context), server-name-hash-bucket-size (computed from the longest host), disable-ipv6-dns (computed from pod IPv6 support), auth-signin-redirect-param rd (template fallback).

Docs conflicts kept as-is: configmap.md says ssl-redirect uses 301 while http-redirect-code defaults to 308; the http2-max-requests section points to upstream-keepalive-requests while its table note and NGINX point to keepalive_requests (keep-alive-requests); jaeger-debug-header default is uber-debug-id in the table but jaeger-debug-id in its section and the old code comment; the table misspells jaeger-tracer-baggage-header-prefix as jaeger-trace-baggage-header-prefix; deprecation notes say 'will be removed in 1.3.0' but the keys still exist at v1.15.1.

klog flags come from the klog v2.140.0 source and a grep of ingress-nginx's own packages; the real binary's --help was not run, so flags registered by transitive dependencies at init time cannot be fully excluded (UNVERIFIED).

Group placement judgment calls: use-port-in-redirects G2; auth-snippet G3 (auth-* rule) and modsecurity-snippet G9 although both are snippets; fastcgi-* G9; disable-proxy-intercept-errors G6; removed global-rate-limit* annotations in G5 (explicitly named there) although the G9 rule covers removed keys; ConfigMap rate-limit keys in G12b and retries in G11; global-auth-snippet G12a while the other global-auth-* keys are G12b.

Risk levels of removed annotations are the last ones seen (v1.11.8 for global-rate-limit*, v1.9.4 for OpenTracing); the influxdb keys and secure-verify-ca-secret predate the risk system and have none.
The AKS application routing add-on may run a different ingress-nginx version than v1.15.1 (covered by F2/F8); key support in that managed controller was not verified here.
The experimental cmd/dataplane binary in the repository was not inventoried; only the nginx-ingress-controller binary from cmd/nginx is covered.
